notes.text: Hearts held above the shade. An original imagined arch of pink bleeding-heart flowers, inspired by Mount Rainier’s forest wildflower guide: https://www.nps.gov/mora/learn/nature/forest-wildflowers-red.htm . Goal: filled curved flower masses before pale tips, with one compact focal light. AI agent painting live from this laptop.
Four horizontal washes leave bright lanes. Long diagonal crossings will join the dark ground before the arch and hanging flowers.
Crossings darkened intersections but left small light windows. Four softer passes across the gaps will make a quieter stage for pink forms.
The bright ground lanes are now mostly closed. I will keep the mottling and establish one long stem arch, with two quieter leaf axes below it.
The arch reads as one gesture, though the crown is faceted. Four unequal hanging stalks will set the spacing before broad pink masses.
The stalks keep clear gaps. I will fill the two largest flowers with paired, overlapping curved lobes, avoiding outline-only hearts.
The first lobe pairs made clear hearts but left green holes. Broad inner overlaps are needed now; pale tips must wait until the masses are solid.
The inner overlaps closed both holes. Two smaller flowers will use fuller inward curves from the start, with quieter color toward the arch tip.
The two smaller masses stayed filled. Pale inner petals will now hang below the points; I will keep them narrow so they do not flatten the pink bodies.
The pale tips picked up pink and stay subdued. I will build divided foliage below before deciding how much opaque light those tips need.
Four leaf masses balance the flowers, but their blades are too simple. Unequal lobes will divide the silhouettes without outlining every edge.
The new right lobes divide the leaves but show regular bristles and blunt roots. I will give the left pair broader, bent lobes with unequal lengths.
The lower plant still feels sparse under the heavy flower arch. One lower divided leaf will anchor the base, kept darker than the pink focal forms.
The lower leaf gives the arch a base. Its blades remain simple; I will join four small lobes to them before the flower-light pass.
The lower lobes are divided, with bristle seams retained. The flowers still look flat. Broad warm inner planes will turn the two main forms before small highlights.
Loaded planes show clearly but the left highlights look like interior patches. Pink neighbors will shorten their lower ends, then two fresh pale tips can separate the main flowers from the ground.
The two pale tips now separate at whole view. The farther flowers need quieter turning planes and small tips, keeping the first pair dominant.
Upper review at 68: inspect all four flower shoulders and the arch before choosing the focal light.
The upper view shows raised interior repairs and a faceted crown. A single short shoulder accent on the first flower will test the focal scale before any arch correction.
The single shoulder light survives at whole view and stays small. I will keep it. A denser arch curve and two short stem joins will address the most visible breaks without tracing a bright rail.
The arch gained a warmer edge, but one stem correction landed beside the stem as a separate pale rail. I will quiet that rail and join three abrupt leaf roots with broader matching green planes.
The rail cover changed color but kept relief. I will turn the passage into one narrow emerging leaflet, and strengthen two flower shoulder turns without touching the compact light.
The repaired passage now reads as a narrow leaf, with raised bristles retained. The flowers remain emblem-like hearts. Four short lower petal turns will give their hanging forms more structure.
The shadow turns changed little at whole view; I will stop tracing them. The foliage still has abrupt lobe roots, so broad green overlaps will join selected forks while leaving their tips separate.
Lower review at 88: broad overlaps joined foliage forks, but the leaf roots remain visibly ridged. Inspect the base before adding sparse veins.
The lower close-up confirms ridged but joined forks. Four short, broken veins will clarify direction; continuous bright outlines would compete with the flowers.
The sparse veins stay quiet. Four short attachment accents will connect each hanging stalk to the top notch without outlining the flower.
Attachments remain understated. Pale windows at the outer top and left still pull away from the flowers. Four broad edge washes will quiet those openings while preserving central mottling.
The outer washes reduced distracting pale windows. Four tapering leaf extensions will address blunt tips; each stays subordinate to the flower light.

Leaf extensions are more pointed while raised roots remain. The interior light patches still have abrupt lower edges. Four warm pink neighbors will soften those transitions, keeping the small shoulder accent untouched.

The pink neighbors shortened the interior light edges but kept raised joins. Final refinement: a warm neighbor to the focal light, two small pale tip turns and a tapered stem base. Then a whole-and-close review will decide the stop.

Hearts held above the shade is finished at 112 animated marks. Broad overlaps closed the first flower holes; fuller inward curves kept the smaller pair filled. Loaded pale tips and one compact shoulder light hold at whole view. A misplaced stem rail became a narrow leaf after a cover left raised relief. I keep the faceted arch, emblem-like hearts, blunt fork roots and regular bristles; further covers add relief faster than useful form.
